To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the oxygen uptake of nickel catalysts supported on SiO2, Al2O3, TiO2, Nb2O5, Zr2O5, V2O5 and ZnO is strongly affected by the interaction of nickel particles with the support and the support itself.
the oxygen chemisorption on supported nickel catalysts is affected by the nature of the support.
the oxygen chemisorption of the supported nickel catalysts is strongly dependent on their supports.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the catalytic activity of supported nickel catalysts in the reaction of the reductive amination with diethylene glycol, as a function of the nature of the supports and the pretreatment of the catalysts.
the synthesis of new catalysts and the development of new methods for the synthesis of organic molecules.
the preparation, characterization and evaluation of a series of unsupported and supported Ni catalysts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxygen chemisorption on supported nickel catalysts is not a suitable technique for the determination of their active sites, but it is useful for comparing their relative activity.
the catalytic activity in the reductive amination is directly related to the oxygen chemisorption capacity, and that this is a function of the nature and the amount of the support.
oxygen chemisorption at -78 ° C is a useful technique for characterization of nickel catalysts, but the results obtained must be interpreted with care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oxygen uptake is not a good indicator for catalytic activity of nickel supported on different oxides.
oxygen uptake of the catalysts is a good measure of their activity in the reductive amination reaction.
the catalytic activity in the reaction of the reductive amination was found to be in the following order: Ni/TiO 2 > Ni/Nb 2 O 2 = Ni/SiO 2 ≈ Ni/ZrO 2 >Ni/Al 2 O 4 > Ni/ZnO ≈ Ni/V 2 O 6.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxygen chemisorption is a useful tool to predict the activity of supported nickel catalysts.
the catalytic properties of the nickel catalysts depend on their surface oxygen coverage and the nature of the support.
oxygen chemisorption is a good indicator of the catalytic performance of the nickel catalyst.
